contests.title: Columbus Issue 8 — City Council District Elections (By Petition)

provenance.quote: This proposed charter amendment would limit the ability to vote for candidates for Columbus City Council to only those electors living within the districts that those candidates seek to represent. The amendment specifies that ballots within council districts will include both citywide races as well as the district race. The amendment allows for the initiation of a recall election of a council district representative if a petition is submitted bearing the signatures of the electors of that district in an amount that is at least fifteen (15%) percent of the votes cast within the district in the preceding mayoral election. Shall the proposed charter amendment be approved?

contests.title: Columbus Issue 9 — City Council District and At-Large Elections

provenance.quote: This proposed charter amendment would limit the ability to vote for candidates for Columbus City Council to only those electors living within the districts that those candidates seek to represent. The amendment adds two (2) at-large council representatives to be elected in 2027 and seated in 2028, and an additional two (2) at-large council representatives to be elected in 2029 and seated in 2030. All at-large council representatives will be elected for four (4) year terms. The amendment includes provisions for transitioning from the current nine (9) member Council to an eleven (11) member Council and then subsequently to a thirteen (13) member Council, allowing for the ongoing staggering of terms. The amendment allows councilmembers representing districts whose boundaries are redrawn but who still have at least two years remaining in their term to serve the remainder of their term representing a newly-drawn district. The amendment specifies that candidates for council district seats must have resided within their district for at least one year prior to the primary election. The amendment calls for a redraw of the current council district map to occur in 2027, and increases the maximum population variance between districts from 1% to 7.5%. The amendment updates the vote requirements for expelling and/or removing councilmembers for misconduct, malfeasance, misfeasance, or nonfeasance. The amendment updates the expulsion vote threshold for conduct from “six” to “2/3rds,” and the expulsion vote for absences from “three-fifths” to “2/3rds.” The amendment updates the charter to reflect the minimum number of councilmembers necessary to achieve a quorum for the purposes of meeting for business. The amendment increases the number of affirmative votes that would be needed to adopt ordinances or resolutions in concert with expanding the size of the legislature. The amendment specifies that candidates for district councilmember must collect at least 150 signatures of electors from within their district, and that at-large candidates must collect at least 250 signatures of electors from within the city limits. The amendment specifies that ballots within council districts will include both citywide races as well as the district race. The amendment allows for the initiation of a recall election of a council district representative if a petition is submitted bearing the signatures of the electors of that district in an amount equal to or greater than fifteen (15%) percent of the votes cast within the district in the preceding mayoral election. The amendment allows for the initiation of a recall election of an at-large representative if a petition is submitted bearing the signatures of the electors citywide in an amount equal to or greater than fifteen (15%) percent of the votes cast within the district in the preceding mayoral election. Shall the proposed charter amendment be approved?

measures.questionText:
Proposed Constitutional Amendment
TO REQUIRE VOTERS TO PRESENT PHOTO
IDENTIFICATION IN ORDER TO VOTE
Proposed by Joint Resolution of the General Assembly
To enact Section 5 of Article V of the Constitution
of the State of Ohio
A majority yes vote is required for the adoption of Section 5.
This proposed amendment would:
• Require voters to present an approved form of government-
issued photo identification in order to vote.
• Allow state law to provide for an alternative method of
verifying a voter’s identity for a voter who has a sincere
religious objection to being photographed and, therefore,
does not possess an approved form of government-issued
photo identification.
• Require that voters who do not vote in person provide an
approved form of government-issued photo identification,
unless the law authorizes those persons to vote by providing a
signature and at least one other specified unique identifier.
• Define approved forms of government-issued photo
identification as an unexpired Ohio driver license or state
identification card; a United States passport or passport card;
or a United States military identification card, Ohio National
Guard identification card, or United States Department of
Veterans Affairs identification card.
If approved, the amendment shall take effect immediately.
A “YES” vote means approval of the amendment.
A “NO” vote means disapproval of the amendment.
SHALL THE AMENDMENT BE APPROVED?

measures.questionText: This proposed charter amendment would limit the ability to vote for candidates for Columbus City Council to only those electors living within the districts that those candidates seek to represent. The amendment adds two (2) at-large council representatives to be elected in 2027 and seated in 2028, and an additional two (2) at-large council representatives to be elected in 2029 and seated in 2030. All at-large council representatives will be elected for four (4) year terms. The amendment includes provisions for transitioning from the current nine (9) member Council to an eleven (11) member Council and then subsequently to a thirteen (13) member Council, allowing for the ongoing staggering of terms. The amendment allows councilmembers representing districts whose boundaries are redrawn but who still have at least two years remaining in their term to serve the remainder of their term representing a newly-drawn district. The amendment specifies that candidates for council district seats must have resided within their district for at least one year prior to the primary election. The amendment calls for a redraw of the current council district map to occur in 2027, and increases the maximum population variance between districts from 1% to 7.5%. The amendment updates the vote requirements for expelling and/or removing councilmembers for misconduct, malfeasance, misfeasance, or nonfeasance. The amendment updates the expulsion vote threshold for conduct from “six” to “2/3rds,” and the expulsion vote for absences from “three-fifths” to “2/3rds.” The amendment updates the charter to reflect the minimum number of councilmembers necessary to achieve a quorum for the purposes of meeting for business. The amendment increases the number of affirmative votes that would be needed to adopt ordinances or resolutions in concert with expanding the size of the legislature. The amendment specifies that candidates for district councilmember must collect at least 150 signatures of electors from within their district, and that at-large candidates must collect at least 250 signatures of electors from within the city limits. Source: https://www.ohiosos.gov/assets/dir2026-45-form-of-the-official-ballot-for-the-november%203-general-election.pdf

Governor and Lieutenant Governor joint tickets are retained as one choice exactly as certified. Valid write-in tickets and Senate candidates are included; the directive does not print their party labels.

BA-01: County-certified lists and official sample ballots now supply all 15 U.S. House, 17 elected state Senate and 99 Ohio House districts, plus the statewide contests. Franklin countywide races and Columbus Issues 8 and 9 are held. Remaining county, city, school, special-district and precinct-level measures are still being acquired; the full 43215 sample ballot and live reader page have not yet been verified.

BA-01: Official sample ballots and certified lists add local Cuyahoga, Hamilton, Summit and Montgomery contests. Current Ohio Revised Code2501.01 establishes county membership in appellate districts. Remaining county, city, school, special-district and precinct-local measure coverage and full43215 paper/live verification remain open.
